what: PG&E delivers electricity and natural gas across northern and central California, serving around 16 million people. It emerged from bankruptcy in 2020 after its equipment was found to have started catastrophic wildfires.
customers: Households, businesses and a growing number of data centres across northern and central California.
moat: A delivery monopoly across a large and wealthy part of California, with rates set by state regulators.
risks: Wildfire liability remains the central risk and California law makes utilities liable even without negligence
Debt of about $63 billion is among the largest of any US utility
Burying power lines is extremely expensive and progress is slow
California political pressure over electricity bills limits rate increases
opportunities: Analysts see about 29% upside from current levels
The California wildfire fund provides a buffer against catastrophic claims
Data centre demand in its territory raises long-term load growth
watch: Wildfire mitigation progress, undergrounding miles completed, and regulatory decisions.
